headline: Middle East conflict and climate deterioration push up garment production costs; clothing prices expected to rise slightly this autumn and soar next spring and summer
summary: Energy price increases and supply chain disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict, plus the expected El Niño, are pushing up garment manufacturing input costs. Clothing prices are expected to rise slightly this autumn and more sharply next spring and summer.
why: Garment manufacturing is a major export industry for Bangladesh, and its cost structure feeds into global apparel prices and retailer margins.
